newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says tax cuts will aid pension scheme.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says tax cuts will aid pension scheme.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday the government's planned tax cuts would aid a compulsory superannuation scheme.
Peters on Tuesday said that the state-run penion scheme could be abandoned in favour of private schemes if the public votes in favour of compulsory superannuation in the September referendum.
If the scheme is voted in, it will come into force on July 1 next year and. By 2002, contributions will be levied at 8.0 percent of assessable income -- earnings and dividends.
Peters, interviewed on Radio New Zealand, was asked how low income earners could afford the scheme.
"We are going to give them an eight percent tax cut and ask them to assign that tax cut to a savings scheme, so they can afford it," Peters replied.

Peters was also asked if the tax cuts did not come through. "We are about to demonstrate that we can deliver those tax cuts and in this budget we will announce the next three percent tax cut and then, after that, we will progress on to 8.0 percent," he said.
